content.value_statement: Responsive interfaces often fail across phones, tablets, and desktops. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for mobile-first layouts, breakpoints, and touch-friendly UI.
actual_capabilities: Applies mobile-first layout guidance for phone, tablet, and desktop views.
Guides media query and breakpoint choices for adaptive interfaces.
Compares relative sizing units such as rem, em, percent, viewport units, and pixels.
Highlights touch target, image, asset, and typography concerns for responsive work.
Supports debugging layout issues at specific viewport sizes.
limitations: The skill is guidance only and does not include a runnable testing tool.
The detailed standard is referenced outside the skill file, so packaged installs may lack that content.
It does not define framework-specific components beyond mentioning Tailwind breakpoints.
It cannot verify visual quality without a browser or screenshot workflow.

use_cases.title: Plan Adaptive Pages
use_cases.description: Define a mobile-first page structure before writing layout styles.

use_cases.title: Review Responsive Components
use_cases.description: Check spacing, typography, touch targets, and content priority across viewport sizes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Viewport Test Notes
use_cases.description: Identify mobile, tablet, and desktop checks for a new interface.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Mobile Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-responsive skill. Help me plan a mobile-first layout for [page name] with key sections, content priority, and desktop expansion.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-responsive skill. Review [component description] for breakpoints, relative units, touch targets, image sizing, and small-screen behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Breakpoints
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-responsive skill. Create a breakpoint strategy for [application area] that covers mobile, tablet, desktop, and large display behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Responsive Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-responsive skill. Audit [workflow or screen set] for layout risks across devices and give prioritized fixes without adding unrelated redesigns.

output_examples.input: Make a dashboard usable on phones and desktop monitors.
output: Start with a single-column mobile layout and expand to multi-column views on wider screens.
Keep primary actions visible, use relative spacing, and verify touch targets on small screens.
Test key breakpoints where tables, charts, and filters change structure.

output_examples.input: Review a product card list for responsive issues.
output: Check that cards stack cleanly on mobile and avoid cramped two-column layouts.
Use fluid media sizing so images stay proportional across viewport widths.
Confirm titles, prices, and action buttons remain readable and easy to tap.

output_examples.input: Plan responsive typography for a marketing page.
output: Use relative font units and define size changes at meaningful content breakpoints.
Keep line length readable on desktop and avoid oversized headings on phones.
Test text wrapping for long labels, headings, and calls to action.

best_practices: Start with the smallest viewport and add layout complexity as space increases.
Choose breakpoints based on content needs, not only common device widths.
Test touch targets, text wrapping, images, and navigation at each important width.
anti_patterns: Do not design only for desktop and shrink the interface afterward.
Do not rely on fixed pixel widths for core layout containers.
Do not hide important content on mobile without a product reason.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan and review responsive frontend layouts across mobile, tablet, and desktop screens.

faq.question: Does it generate production CSS by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides responsive design guidance that an agent can apply while editing code.

faq.question: Can it help with Tailwind projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill mentions Tailwind breakpoints and can guide responsive utility choices.

faq.question: Does it include automated browser testing?
faq.answer: No. Use a browser, screenshots, or test tooling to verify the final layout.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should authors fix before publishing?
faq.answer: They should package the referenced responsive standard inside the skill directory.
